title: What If Every Termite Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every termite vanished? Their combined weight is about the same as all humans put together.
Across the tropics, termites are credited with more than 55 percent of all decomposition.
Termites fix nitrogen, turn over soil and create nutrient hotspots whose effects on soil can last for decades.
They also release methane: about 15 million tonnes a year, roughly 2 percent of the world's total.
Fewer than 10 percent of the roughly 3,000 termite species are pests. The rest simply recycle dead plants.
Remove them and the world loses a methane source, but also the main recyclers of the tropics.
